scene_generation_pipeline: Trimesh analytic stable poses and 2D footprint packing -> Isaac Sim 5.0 short stability filter -> camera capture

dataset_split.policy: Scene-disjoint 16/2/2 split. All eight camera views of one physical scene remain in the same split to prevent layout leakage.

table.source: DexGraspNet 2.0 paper and supplement: objects are placed within an approximately 30 cm x 50 cm tabletop/area. The 2 cm thickness and tabletop-centred world origin are adapter conventions.

candidate_sampling.source: Adapter method: Trimesh 4.12.2 compute_stable_poses provides quasi-static support poses; Shapely 2D convex footprints are packed inside the paper-sized tabletop. This is not the unreleased modified DREDS generator.

stable_pose_scene_generation.source: Adapter values. Stable support transforms and quasi-static landing probabilities come from trimesh.poses.compute_stable_poses. Each transformed mesh is represented by its XY convex footprint. The anchor object is random and remaining objects are packed largest-first for efficiency. Candidate scenes cycle through uniform, compact and spread layout families; compact/spread modes randomly select within the best 15 percent rather than taking a deterministic argmax. Candidate layouts must differ by at least 12 mm RMS in their labelled-object pairwise XY-distance signatures. All modes retain a 5 mm pairwise clearance and 15 mm table-edge margin, then place objects 1 mm above the table for a short Isaac Sim 5.0 verification.

physics.source: mass=0.1 kg and friction=0.2 follow DexGraspNet 2.0 evaluation settings; solver/contact details are adapter values

stability.source: Adapter acceptance contract. Analytic candidates start 1 mm above their stable support plane. Isaac allows up to 2 s for settling, records the velocity-quiet diagnostic, and then accepts only if every object moves at most 2 mm and rotates at most 2 degrees over a separate 1 s observation. Exact mesh vertices must remain inside the tabletop and no more than 3 mm below its contact plane. Exact scene-stability thresholds are not published.

camera.pose_source: open-source GraspNet scene_0000/realsense: T_table_camera = cam0_wrt_table @ camera_poses[index]
camera.intrinsics_source: open-source GraspNet scene_0000/realsense/camK.npy, converted to Isaac/Omniverse's supported pinhole form by averaging fx/fy and centering cx/cy
camera.placement_note: Official rotations are retained. Translation is fitted along each optical axis so the centred 0.50 x 0.30 x 0.20 m tabletop workspace remains visible with a 5 percent image border.
camera.coordinate_contract: OpenCV optical frame: +x image-right, +y image-down, +z camera-forward; extrinsics is T_world_camera

workspace.sampling: Match src/utils/pc.py:get_workspace_mask: transform visible object points to world/table coordinates, expand their axis-aligned bounds by 0.02 m, retain finite depth points in the box, then sample with replacement exactly as official dataset.py.

grasp_label_generation.pregrasp_axis: for each q_grasp, compute the r_base_link direction from the semantic palm center to the thumb/index-tip midpoint; PREGRASP retreats 0.10 m opposite that reviewed Wuji2 tiger-mouth approach direction
grasp_label_generation.collision_source: The strict 2.5 mm clearance is the open-source dex_graspness.py default. SimulationEvaluator constructs pregrasp by opening fingertips 25 mm and retreating 100 mm. The official repository consumes precomputed collision_label files but does not include their generator; this adapter evaluates the same signed-distance inequality against 1000 deterministic surface samples per scene object, matching the official preprocessing default object_points=1000.
grasp_label_generation.graspness_source: Exact defaults and equations reproduced from DexGraspNet2/src/preprocess/dex_graspness.py: 1000 complete-surface points, 30 degree cone half-angle, 2 cm height band, angular half decay at 10 degrees, height half decay at 1.5 cm, and 10**(-150*distance) accumulation around each grasp reference point.
grasp_label_generation.source: DexGraspNet 2.0 supplement filters single-object grasps at less than 2 mm hand-object penetration after six-axis gravity validation with friction 0.2. The Wuji2 network target is the optimizer posture before Isaac force tightening; the force-adjusted posture is retained only as validation provenance.

network_training.training_policy: Train from random initialization for 5000 iterations first. Extend toward 10000 only if held-out validation/inference still improves; do not copy the paper's 50000 iterations onto this much smaller teaching subset.
network_training.source: DexGraspNet2/configs/network/train_dex_ours.yaml uses voxel_size=0.005, sample_total=128, k=64, max_point_dis=0.006, feature_dim=512 and joint_num=16. Only joint_num changes to 20 for Wuji2.

enhanced_palm_path_filter.target_object_policy: excluded because target contact/enclosure is intentional
enhanced_palm_path_filter.method: Exact finite line-segment versus triangle-mesh intersection using the semantic palm center at official-style pregrasp and final grasp. Both endpoints must remain at least 2.5 mm above the scene_manifest tabletop top_z plane.
enhanced_palm_path_filter.scope_warning: This checks only the zero-radius semantic-palm centerline. It is stronger than the published pregrasp endpoint filter but is not a full swept-volume collision guarantee for the articulated hand.
